indicators.note: the fish's letters stretch across, and so enclose, the river's abbreviation

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish

explanation.surface: An angler notes a dull-coloured flatfish swimming across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dull and colourless, a plain synonym pairing.

indicators.note: the north letter falls within, in the middle of, the storm word

parts.note: to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: A ship's compass points north in the middle of a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass' looks like the navigating instrument but means scope or extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of scope or extent, the reach of something, is a synonym.

parts.note: brave means courageous
Dvorak's Ninth Symphony is known as From the New World

explanation.surface: Someone praises a symphony as new and bold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the adjective meaning new, but it is the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldous Huxley's 1932 dystopian book is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Kind female by a church font

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A gentle woman stands beside a church font, ready for a christening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'font' looks like the baptismal basin in a church, but it is the printer's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a font is one style and size of lettering, also called a typeface.

clue.text: Time to remove unwanted plants in river

parts.note: to weed is to clear unwanted plants

explanation.surface: A gardener says it's time to clear the weeds growing in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river on the border between Scotland and England, an example.

parts.note: a play is a drama
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A playwright features in a youth production.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fenced area where a baby or toddler plays safely, an enclosure for the very young.

definitions.meaning: Sir Topham Hatt, the stout railway manager in the Thomas the Tank Engine stories; the 's stands for 'is'
a slimming diet regulates how much fat one carries

explanation.surface: Asks whether a storybook railway chief is on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'boss' is short for 'is', linking the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotund manager in the Thomas the Tank Engine books; also, whimsically, anything that keeps body fat in check.

clue.text: Combo's leader plays new love song

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
new suggests the letters are made over afresh, so they are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scores, the letter O

explanation.surface: The band's frontman performs a fresh love song.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean style of song from Trinidad, so an example of a song.

indicators.note: to manoeuvre is to move things around, so these letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: US military exercises were conducted away from public view.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal phrase for proceedings held in private, away from the public and press.

indicators.note: signals that a word heard spoken is what is wanted, its sound matching a differently spelt one

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A detective is said to shadow someone, or perhaps it is just a rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative or yarn is a straightforward synonym for a story.

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member, of the body
a close is an end or conclusion

explanation.surface: A list of three nouns: an important club member reaches the closing stage.
explanation.definitionFit: On a map or chart, the key explaining its symbols is called the legend.

clue.text: Young man may get praise skipping university

indicators.note: the university letter is passed over, left out of the praise word

parts.note: to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: A young man might earn compliments without going to college.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy or youth is commonly called this, a synonym.

indicators.note: the pint's abbreviation is placed following the concert word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a swift beer once the concert is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean done without delay; a timely, speedy response is a synonym pairing.

clue.text: Put off M1 before race, leading to conviction

parts.note: to deter is to put someone off
the digit 1 is read as the letter I, giving MI
a race of people can be a nation

explanation.surface: Discouraged from the M1 motorway before a race, someone shows real resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; here it is just the letters M and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmness of purpose or resolve is a synonym for conviction in the sense of strong belief.

indicators.note: suspect letters are doubtful or not right, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the holiday chalet is respectable.
explanation.definitionFit: Morally right and fair is a synonym for decent.

clue.text: Unfortunately butter possibly going up, and dessert wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of misfortune
a ram, which butts, is one kind of butter

explanation.surface: Sadly the price of butter is rising, and so is that of sweet wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' looks like the dairy spread but means something that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from Sicily, often drunk with or used in desserts.

clue.text: Fellow brought over gives slight bow

indicators.note: turned over so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A college fellow, invited over, bows politely.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief inclination of the head is a small bow or greeting.

clue.text: One pointing out group one disapproves of?

definitions.meaning: a person who points things out, someone who displays them
British slang for a contemptible lot

explanation.surface: A disapproving guide points out the unruly bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one who shows; in British slang, a useless or despised crowd of people.

clue.text: Sacked from Orton play (Joe's last), departs

parts.note: Loot is a 1965 comedy by the playwright Joe Orton

indicators.note: Joe's last is the final letter of the name Joe, the possessive merely linking it

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Someone was fired from an Orton production and walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Orton was an English playwright; 'Joe' here is his first name, whose last letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, so sacked means plundered, a synonym.

indicators.note: the American abbreviation is placed following the fortune word

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: An American seeks a plant after making his fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A water lily of Asia is the plant meant, an example.

clue.text: Get rid of former PM, half-heartedly

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: one of the two central letters, half the heart, is dropped

parts.note: Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister is half-hearted about getting rid of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw out or eject is a synonym for getting rid of.

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A dent or scratch shows on the family's second car.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish left on the skin by a healed wound is a mark.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered or put wrong, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creature bounded out of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A deer-like hoofed creature of Africa and Asia is one example of an animal.

clue.text: Good boys protecting kid in best clothes

indicators.note: the boys' letters wrap around and shield the kid word

parts.note: lads are boys
to kid is to tease, which is also to rag

explanation.surface: Well-behaved boys shield a young child while dressed in their Sunday best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the verb meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal phrase for one's finest outfit, worn on a special occasion.

clue.text: Part of conditional release the old man ignored

indicators.note: the father's word is left out, disregarded, from the longer word

parts.note: parole is early release from prison on conditions
PA is a familiar word for one's father, the old man

explanation.surface: A prisoner's parole was granted, though Dad paid no attention.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's part in a play is the character played, a synonym.
